executive_summary.question: Under the BSA, when is a document considered to be in 'proper custody' for the purposes of the presumption of genuineness?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
Under the BSA (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam), a document is regarded as being in **proper custody** for the purpose of the presumption of genuineness when:

- It is kept **in the place where it is required to be kept**, and  
- It is **looked after by the person with whom such document is required to be kept**.  

Additionally, custody will not be considered improper if it can be shown that the document **had a legitimate origin**, or if the circumstances of the case make that origin probable.  

This definition is provided in the Explanation to the relevant section (see the passage discussing sections 80 and 92)【f940d7fd-8aa1-4435-ae63-7b1fad4e66a3】.

evidence_analysis.supporting_evidence:

said to be in proper custody if they are in the place in which, and looked after by the person
with whom such document is required to be kept; but no custody is improper if it is proved
to have had a legitimate origin, or the circumstances of the particular case are such as to
